rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should explore a promising baseline. config_001 tests a transformer-based image-only model with resnet50, which balances complexity and potential performance. This clarifies the effectiveness of transformer aggregation and resnet50 for image data, providing foundational insights before exploring multimodal configurations.

The existing evidence shows that image-only models (config_001) achieve low accuracy (0.2239). This experiment tests a multimodal approach with multiprofile settings, using scgpt (a more sophisticated RNA encoder) and imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. This clarifies whether combining modalities with advanced encoders and fusion improves performance, addressing key uncertainties about RNA/image synergy and aggregation methods.

The existing evidence shows config_003 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.542 validation accuracy. This experiment tests transformer aggregation and concat fusion (config_007) with the same RNA/image encoders, exploring if these changes could improve performance. It directly builds on config_003's strong foundation while testing critical design choices (aggregation/fusion) that may yield higher accuracy.

Existing evidence shows config_003 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.542 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping scgpt and imagenet_vit_l, which could improve performance. It directly builds on the top-performing config_003 by exploring a key design choice (aggregation method) that might yield better results.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with scgpt RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders (config_003) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA and resnet50 image encoders with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, exploring if alternative encoders and aggregation methods can improve performance. It balances exploration of new encoder combinations while building on the success of multimodal approaches.

The existing evidence shows config_045 (0.713 accuracy) is the top performer using scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests a similar setup with pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, and concat fusion, which could clarify if the RNA encoder or image encoder choice is critical. It balances exploration (testing different encoders) with exploitation (maintaining transformer aggregation) to further refine the optimal configuration.

The existing evidence shows config_045 (multimodal, scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation method but with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion. It clarifies whether the fusion method significantly impacts performance, while maintaining the strong foundation of the top-performing configuration. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (like config_045) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests a similar configuration but with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, which could improve performance by leveraging a more powerful visual feature extractor. It clarifies whether the image encoder choice is critical for further gains, balancing exploitation of current trends with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that config_038 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_040) could improve performance, clarifying if the current best's aggregation/fusion choices are optimal. This balances exploitation of promising components with exploration of alternative design choices under the limited budget.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_038) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.725). This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, exploring whether alternative encoder pairs and fusion methods could further improve performance. It balances exploitation (using transformer aggregation) with exploration (testing different encoders/fusion) to reduce uncertainty about optimal design choices.
